messages.author: edbb58ff07e2feec
messages.subject: mixed item types
parts:
Hello Phil,

I am using mirt to examine measurement invariance of a literacy test for different subgroups. I have 5 factors. I haven't been able to even confirm configural invariance, and I think it may have something to do with using mixed items, as I have both dichotomous and polytomous data. 

When I run the following code, I get several  "In model.elements(model = model, itemtype = itemtype, factorNames = factorNames,  : NAs introduced by coercion". 

itemT <- rep('2PL', 50)
itemT[19] <- 'graded'
itemT[40:50] <- 'graded'
mod<- mirt(L1.2, Q2, itemtype=itemT, method="MCEM")

Am I running the mixed items incorrectly? Any help would be appreciated!

Jeanne Sinclair

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: mixed item types
parts:
Seems correct to me. Are you certain that it's the itemtype argument that's causing the error to arise? Also, the default itemtypes in mirt are automatically graded/2PL, so this vector definition is not strictly necessary. 

Phil

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: mixed item types
parts:
The problem could have to do with supplying items with decimals. IRT models typically are for categorical models only (that's not strictly true, but in mirt it is), so it's likely that including items with decimals is confusing the internal mechanics when trying to organise the items as a set of dummy coding matrices. That would be my first guess, but it might be something else.  

Phil
